candidate.answerReason: For every real x, x²≥0 and hence -x²≤0. Equality is attained at x=0, so the maximum is 0.

methods.label: Use the sign of a square
methods.explanation: The squared term is nonnegative, so with a negative sign in front, the maximum is \(0\), attained at \(x=0\).
methods.levelReason: Nonnegativity of a square and reversal of an inequality under negation give a complete elementary argument.
